title: Regular ring maps are stable under finite type base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ be a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of commutative rings (flat, with every fibre ring $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$), and let $R\to R'$ be a ring map of finite type, i.e. $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Then the base change $R'\to\Lambda\otimes_RR'$, $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$, is a regular ring map. (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C1.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change, 'Regular maps and base change'), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07C1; its proof uses Algebra lemma-flat-base-change, lemma-Noetherian-field-extension and lemma-geometrically-regular. Used in the proof of Proposition 07PV ('as a localization of a base change of the regular ring map R -> R^').

proof.text: (Flatness.) Write $\Lambda'=\Lambda\otimes_RR'$, an $R'$-algebra through $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$. Since $R\to\Lambda$ is regular, $\Lambda$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. By flat base change [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] (with the ring map $R\to R'$ and $M=\Lambda$) the $R'$-module $R'\otimes_R\Lambda$ is flat, and the symmetry $\Lambda\otimes_RR'\cong R'\otimes_R\Lambda$, $\lambda\otimes r'\mapsto r'\otimes\lambda$, is an isomorphism of $R'$-modules; so $R'\to\Lambda'$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07C1, first sentence (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HI lemma-flat-base-change)

proof.text: (The residue fields.) Fix a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ and let $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak p')\subset R$, $f:R\to R'$ the structure map; $\mathfrak p$ is prime ($1\notin\mathfrak p$, and $ab\in\mathfrak p$ gives $f(a)f(b)\in\mathfrak p'$). Let $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\pi':R'\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be the canonical maps [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\bar f:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ the induced map, $\overline{a/s}\mapsto\overline{f(a)/f(s)}$; it satisfies $\bar f\circ\pi=\pi'\circ f$ (both send $a$ to the class of $f(a)/1$), so the two $R$-algebra structures on $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, through $\pi'\circ f$ and through $\bar f\circ\pi$, are the same. Since $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra, $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is a finitely generated field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ through $\bar f$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated]: $\kappa(\mathfrak p')=\kappa(\mathfrak p)(a_1,\dots,a_m)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07C1, second and third sentences

proof.text: (The fibre ring.) Put $A=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R\Lambda$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra through the first factor; by the symmetry of $\otimes$ it is isomorphic as a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra to the fibre ring $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $R\to\Lambda$ at $\mathfrak p$. Let $F=\Lambda'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be the fibre ring of $R'\to\Lambda'$ at $\mathfrak p'$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra through the second factor. We construct an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebras $F\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A$. First, by symmetry and $\Lambda'\cong R'\otimes_R\Lambda$ (as $R'$-algebras), $F\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_R\Lambda)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R\to S:=R'$, $B:=\Lambda$, the $R'$-algebra $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ via $\pi'$) gives an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebras $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_R\Lambda)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_R\Lambda$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an $R$-algebra through $\pi'\circ f$. Second, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R\to S:=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ via $\pi$, $B:=\Lambda$, the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ via $\bar f$) gives an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebras $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R\Lambda)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_R\Lambda$, where now $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an $R$-algebra through $\bar f\circ\pi$; by Step 2 this is the same $R$-algebra structure as before, so the two right-hand sides are the same ring. Composing, $F\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A$ as $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebras. (This is the displayed identity of the Stacks proof.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07C1, the displayed identity

proof.text: ($F$ is Noetherian.) As $R\to\Lambda$ is regular, the fibre ring $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence its isomorphic copy $A$, is a Noetherian $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra which is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (both properties are defined through the ring structure and the tensor products $k'\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}-$, so they pass along a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra isomorphism). Since $\kappa(\mathfrak p')/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finitely generated field extension (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] (with $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p')$) shows that $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A$ is Noetherian (and regular); so $F$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] by Step 3. (Stacks cites Algebra Lemma Tag 045I lemma-Noetherian-field-extension here; its content is included in the cited node.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07C1, fourth sentence (Algebra, Lemma Tag 045I lemma-Noetherian-field-extension)

proof.text: ($F$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$.) Let $k''/\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. By Step 3, $k''\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p')}F\cong k''\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p')}(\kappa(\mathfrak p')\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R\to S:=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $B:=A$, the $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra $k''$) identifies this ring with $k''\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A$. The field extension $k''/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finitely generated: if $\kappa(\mathfrak p')=\kappa(\mathfrak p)(a_1,\dots,a_m)$ (Step 2) and $e_1,\dots,e_r$ is a $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-basis of $k''$, the subfield $\kappa(\mathfrak p)(a_1,\dots,a_m,e_1,\dots,e_r)$ of $k''$ contains $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ and all $e_j$, hence every $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-linear combination of the $e_j$, i.e. all of $k''$. So [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] (with $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $K=k''$ and the geometrically regular Noetherian $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra $A$ of Step 4) shows that $k''\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}A$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]; regularity (Noetherian, all localizations at primes regular local) passes along ring isomorphisms, so $k''\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p')}F$ is regular. As $k''$ was arbitrary and $F$ is Noetherian (Step 4), $F$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. (Stacks: 'Geometric regularity of the fibres is preserved by Algebra, Lemma 0381', used as (2)=>(1) for $A$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07C1, last sentence (Algebra, Lemma Tag 0381 lemma-geometrically-regular)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $R'\to\Lambda'$ is flat (Step 1), and for every prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ its fibre ring $F=\Lambda'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is Noetherian (Step 4) and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ (Step 5); so $R'\to\Lambda\otimes_RR'$ is a regular ring map by the definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].
